question: In the popular traditions of Vijayanagara, the Deccan Sultans are termed as ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashvapati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the popular traditions of Vijayanagara, the Deccan Sultans were often referred to as **Ashvapati**, which translates to "Lord of Horses".
 
• This term is indicative of the significant role that cavalry played in the military strategies of the Deccan Sultanates.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan Sultanates were frequently in conflict, and the term Ashvapati highlights the martial prowess attributed to the Deccan rulers.
 
• The term was part of a broader set of terminologies used in the militaristic and political lexicon of the time, reflecting the power dynamics and cultural perceptions of the era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I in the Deccan region of South India.
 
• It is renowned for its advanced administration, military conquests, and contributions to art and architecture.
 
• The empire was known for its strong defense mechanisms, including the use of fortified cities and strategic military alliances.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Sultanates:**
 
 
• The Deccan Sultanates were a group of five Muslim-ruled states in Central and South India during the medieval period.
 
• These Sultanates included Bijapur, Golkonda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, and Berar.
 
• They frequently engaged in warfare with the Vijayanagara Empire, leading to a dynamic and often volatile political landscape.
 
 
 
• **Military Strategy:**
 
 
• Cavalry played a crucial role in the military strategies of both the Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan Sultanates.
 
• Horses were considered valuable assets in warfare, influencing the terms used to describe rulers and their military power.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Perceptions:**
 
 
• The terms used to refer to rulers, such as Ashvapati, were reflective of the cultural and military values of the time.
 
• These terminologies provide insight into how power and authority were perceived and communicated within and between different states.
